text: explainers Russians are buying more antidepressants every year. Doctors say that doesn’t necessarily mean more Russians are depressed. 6 cards August 28, 2026, 9:27 pm Contents 1 Russia’s rising antidepressant sales Antidepressant sales in Russia have been growing steadily, a trend the media covers regularly . We decided to look at what may be behind it — and at what people who are about to start taking antidepressants, or to stop, need to know. 2 Demand has gone up because more people are developing depression. Isn’t that it? Not necessarily. Specialists say several factors are at work here. It may in fact be that more people are developing depression: the events of recent years have contributed to that. But antidepressants are also prescribed for other mental disorders — for post-traumatic stress disorder, for example, which can be triggered by war. Over time, more and more people are learning that the symptoms they have are a sign of a mental disorder, and they no longer find it shameful to see a psychiatrist or to take antidepressants. Photograph: Mono County Sheriff Search and Rescue Team US news Volunteers rescue man stuck on 10,000ft-high ledge in Sierra Nevada Climber, stuck on 6in ridge, had veered off treacherous path and ‘any fall would almost certainly be fatal’ Uwa Ede-Osifo Fri 28 Aug 2026 17.30 EDT Last modified on Fri 28 Aug 2026 17.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An ill-fated move left a man stranded on a 6in ledge over 10,000ft off the ground for hours in California’s Sierra Nevada mountain range, before a volunteer rescue team came to his aid. The climber, who has not been publicly identified, had been scaling the Mendenhall couloir, a gully on the face of Laurel mountain, with a friend on Saturday. text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. Russia’s communications watchdog Roskomnadzor has not commented on the outage. One of the region’s most famous tales centers on the “ Altai Princess ” — a permafrost-preserved mummy discovered on the Ukok Plateau in 1993 by a team of Novosibirsk archeologists led by Natalya Polosmak. The finding was hailed at the time as an international sensation. Dated to the 5th century BC, the 25-year-old woman’s waxen skin is covered in vibrant indigo tattoos, and she was buried in a wooden chamber alongside six horses, dressed in silk, wool and felt. But more than three decades later, local shamans are calling for the mummy to be reburied. title: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage
text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. Russia’s communications watchdog Roskomnadzor has not commented on the outage. title: Calls to Rebury a Siberian Mummy Unearth Decades of Distorted History

Ludvig14 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Millions of tourists flock to southern Siberia’s republic of Altai each year, drawn by its dramatic mountain ranges steeped in the legends of the indigenous Altai people. One of the region’s most famous tales centers on the “ Altai Princess ” — a permafrost-preserved mummy discovered on the Ukok Plateau in 1993 by a team of Novosibirsk archeologists led by Natalya Polosmak. title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills One, Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery
text: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills One, Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery Aug. 28, 2026 @supernova_plus / Telegram A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person and sparked a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the city of Yaroslavl, Russian and Ukrainian authorities said Friday. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said one civilian was killed and 27 others were injured after falling drone debris hit an intercity bus. He claimed that 67 Ukrainian drones were downed over the region, but that drone debris fell on residential areas, commercial properties and “industrial infrastructure.” Ukraine’s military said it struck the Slavneft-Yanos refinery, which it said provides fuel and lubricants for the Russian military. title: Car Bomb Kills Military Officer in St. Petersburg
text: Car Bomb Kills Military Officer in St. Petersburg Aug. 28, 2026 @fontankaspb / Telegram A Russian military official has been killed in a car explosion in St. Petersburg, investigators said Thursday, with local media identifying his rank as lieutenant colonel. The blast occurred around 10 a.m. local time near a supermarket in the Shushary neighborhood, the news outlet Fontanka reported. Investigators later confirmed the military official’s death but described the incident only as a “vehicle fire,” not an explosion. They also said his wife, who was also inside the car at the time of the blast, was receiving medical treatment. The Investigation Committee, Russia ’s top investigative body, said it launched a criminal probe into the incident. The exiled news outlet Agentstvo said pro-war Telegram channels identified the victim as 43-year-old Sergei Sechkov. title: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say
text: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say Image source, Getty Images By Jonathan Beale Defence correspondent Published 28 August 2026 Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to avoid a direct military confrontation with Nato, despite increasingly hostile rhetoric aimed at the UK and other allies over their support for Ukraine, Western officials believe. Some reports have suggested the visit by CIA chief John Radcliffe to Moscow this week was, in part, to warn Russia against a possible attack on a member of the Euro-Atlantic military alliance. But the Western officials, who asked not to be named, said recent warnings from Moscow, including that UK forces could be targeted in future or that its weapons factories could be hit, were "nothing new". They were, they suggested, consistent with Russia's military doctrine to apply pressure on the West. The officials suggested that the hostile rhetoric was also a reflection of the growing pressure Putin is facing at home, with slow and costly gains in Ukraine along with the impact of Ukrainian long-range strikes deep inside Russia. title: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test
text: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test Aug. 28, 2026 Russian Defense Ministry Russia’s Defense Ministry announced Friday that it conducted a successful combat training launch of a mobile, solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the northwestern Arkhangelsk region. The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east. Video released by the Defense Ministry showed the missile launch from a forested location. The military said the goal of the launch was to confirm the “tactical, technical and flight characteristics of the missile system.” “All assigned tasks were completed in full,” the ministry said, adding that the ICBM maintained a “flawless trajectory.” It did not identify the missile used in the launch. The Defense Ministry reportedly launched the RS-24 Yars system from Plesetsk to Kura as part of wide-ranging missile forces exercises in mid-May. title: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage
text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. title: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test
text: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test Aug. 28, 2026 Russian Defense Ministry Russia’s Defense Ministry announced Friday that it conducted a successful combat training launch of a mobile, solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the northwestern Arkhangelsk region. The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east. Video released by the Defense Ministry showed the missile launch from a forested location. The military said the goal of the launch was to confirm the “tactical, technical and flight characteristics of the missile system.” “All assigned tasks were completed in full,” the ministry said, adding that the ICBM maintained a “flawless trajectory.” It did not identify the missile used in the launch. The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east. title: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage
text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. Russia’s communications watchdog Roskomnadzor has not commented on the outage. Roskomnadzor has fined Wikipedia multiple times over its refusal to delete articles related to the full-scale invasion of Ukrain

text: Car Bomb Kills Military Officer in St. Petersburg Aug. 28, 2026 @fontankaspb / Telegram A Russian military official has been killed in a car explosion in St. Petersburg, investigators said Thursday, with local media identifying his rank as lieutenant colonel. The blast occurred around 10 a.m. local time near a supermarket in the Shushary neighborhood, the news outlet Fontanka reported. Investigators later confirmed the military official’s death but described the incident only as a “vehicle fire,” not an explosion. title: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say
text: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say Image source, Getty Images By Jonathan Beale Defence correspondent Published 28 August 2026 Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to avoid a direct military confrontation with Nato, despite increasingly hostile rhetoric aimed at the UK and other allies over their support for Ukraine, Western officials believe. Some reports have suggested the visit by CIA chief John Radcliffe to Moscow this week was, in part, to warn Russia against a possible attack on a member of the Euro-Atlantic military alliance. But the Western officials, who asked not to be named, said recent warnings from Moscow, including that UK forces could be targeted in future or that its weapons factories could be hit, were "nothing new". They were, they suggested, consistent with Russia's military doctrine to apply pressure on the West. The officials suggested that the hostile rhetoric was also a reflection of the growing pressure Putin is facing at home, with slow and costly gains in Ukraine along with the impact of Ukrainian long-range strikes deep inside Russia. title: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test
text: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test Aug. 28, 2026 Russian Defense Ministry Russia’s Defense Ministry announced Friday that it conducted a successful combat training launch of a mobile, solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the northwestern Arkhangelsk region. The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east. Video released by the Defense Ministry showed the missile launch from a forested location. The military said the goal of the launch was to confirm the “tactical, technical and flight characteristics of the missile system.” “All assigned tasks were completed in full,” the ministry said, adding that the ICBM maintained a “flawless trajectory.” It did not identify the missile used in the launch. The Defense Ministry reportedly launched the RS-24 Yars system from Plesetsk to Kura as part of wide-ranging missile forces exercises in mid-May. President.gov.ua A judge in Moscow on Friday sentenced Oleksiy Arestovych, a former adviser to the Ukrainian president’s office, to 11 years in prison in absentia after finding him guilty of spreading false information about the Russian military and publicly calling for terrorism. Russian investigators accused Arestovych of publishing false statements about a deadly Russian missile strike on a railway statio n in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk in April 2022. A judge from the Second Western District Military Court delivered the guilty verdict against Arestovych following a closed-door trial. title: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage
text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. Russia’s communications watchdog Roskomnadzor has not commented on the outage. title: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage
text: Access Restored to Wikipedia in Russia After Overnight Outage Aug. 28, 2026 Sirperry1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian users reported widespread outages of Wikipedia early Friday before access was restored later in the day, independent monitoring groups said. Issues with opening the online encyclopedia began shortly after midnight Moscow time. Monitoring services S boy and D owndetector tracked a spike in outage reports across major cities like Moscow, St. Petersburg and Novosibirsk. Users reported that Wikipedia remained accessible when using VPNs. Network testing data from OONI Explorer, the world’s largest open dataset on internet censorship, reportedly showed access anomaly rates for Wikipedia’s Russian-language version briefly hit 100% early Friday, while hitting 75% for the English-language version. Access began to be restored and disruption rates dropped significantly by 10 a.m. Moscow time. The tech platform Habr reported that Wikipedia was inaccessible in Russia for eight hours. Russia’s communications watchdog Roskomnadzor has not commented on the outage.
